professus.definition: professus adj. P. of profiteor, avowed, confessed : culpa, O.: mors, i. e. certain , Ph.

proficiscor.definition: proficīscor fectus, ī, dep. proficio, to set forward, set out, start, go, march, depart : fortasse tu profectus alio fueras, were going somewhere else , T.: cum in Italiam proficisceretur, was about to start , Cs.: Ut…

profligatus.definition: prōflīgātus adj. with sup. P. of profligo, wretched, vile, corrupt, abandoned : iudicia: tu omnium mortalium profligatissime: homines.

profluens.definition: prōfluēns adj. P. of profluo, flowing along : aqua profluens.—As subst f . (sc. aqua), running water : in profluentem deferri.—Fig., of speech, flowing, fluent : genus sermonis: celeritas.

profluentia.definition: prōfluentia ae, f profluens, a flowing forth : loquendi, stream of words .

profundum.definition: profundum ī, n profundus, a depth : esse in profundo (aquae): maris, O.— The depths of the sea, deep sea : ex profundo molem ad caelum erigit, Att. ap. C.: profundo Vela dabit, V.: genitor profundi, i. e. Neptune , O.…

profuse.definition: profūsē adv. with comp. profusus, immoderately, excessively : eo profusius sumptui deditus erat, S.— Confusedly, in disorder : tendentes in castra, L. (al. effuse).

profusus.definition: profūsus adj. P. of profundo.—Of persons, lavish, extravagant, profuse : nepos: alieni appetens, sui profusus, lavish of his own , S.—Of things, extravagant, excessive, profuse : profusis sumptibus vivere: epulae: gen…

progener.definition: prōgener ī, m a grand-daughter's husband, Ta.

progressus2.definition: prōgressus ūs, m pro+GRAD-, a going forward, advance, progress : alqm progressu arcere: progressūs et regressūs constantes (of planets).—Fig., advancement, progress, growth, increase : aetatis: primo progressu, at the…

proiectio.definition: prōiectiō ōnis, f pro+IA-, a throwing forward, stretching out : brachii.

proiectus.definition: prōiectus adj. P. of proicio, stretched out, extended, jutting out, projecting : urbs in altum: saxa, V.— Prostrate, outstretched : ego in antro, V. —Fig., prominent, conspicuous : audacia: cupiditas.— Inclined, addic…

prolixe.definition: prōlixē adv. with comp. prolixus, largely, abundantly, copiously, freely : Capillus passus, T.: id fecit.— Freely, readily, cheerfully, bountifully : Accipit nemo prolixius, entertains more liberally , T.: polliceri: …

promereor.definition: prō-mereor meritus, ērī, dep., to deserve, merit, earn, be worthy: Ita velim me promerentem ames, T.: levius punitus quam sit promeritus: paratiores ad bene de multis promerendum: te numquam negabo (ea) Promeritam, V.

promeritum.definition: prō-meritum ī, n P. n. of promereor, desert, merit : vestrum in nos: deae, O.

prominens.definition: prōminēns entis, adj. P. of promineo, prominent .—As subst n., a projection : in prominenti litoris, Ta.: prominentia montium, Ta.

promisce.definition: prōmiscē adv. promiscus, in common, indiscriminately, indifferently : iudicium promisce stultis ac sapientibus datum: aedificari, i. e. without regard to private ownership of land , L.

promiscue.definition: prōmiscuē adv. promiscuus, in common , promiscuously, confusedly, indiscriminately : (mares et feminae) promiscue in fluminibus perluuntur, Cs.: puberes atque negotiatores interficere, S.

promiscus.definition: prōmiscus adj. pro+MIC-, in common, indiscriminate, promiscuous : usus rerum omnium, L.—As subst n. : nec arma in promisco, i. e. in every man's hands , Ta.— Common, mean : promisca ac vilia mercari, Ta.

promissum.definition: prōmissum ī, n P. n. of promitto, a promise : nostrum: promisso teneri: promissis induxit alquem: deum promisso ludit inani, O.: illis promissis standum non est: promissis manere, V.: Dic aliquid dignum promissis, H.:…

promissus.definition: prōmissus adj. P. of promitto, hanging down, long : coma, L.: capillo esse promisso, Cs.

promota.definition: prōmōta ōrum, n P. of promoveo, preferable things .

prompte.definition: (prōmptē) adv. with comp. 1 promptus, readily, quickly : dare operam, Ta.— Easily : promptius expediam, Iu.—Fig., openly, freely : dicam paulo promptius.

promptus1.definition: prōmptus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of promo, set forth, brought forward, disclosed, exposed, manifest : aliud clausum in pectore, aliud promptum in linguā habere, S.: prompta et aperta: nihil quod non istius cupidit…

promptus2.definition: (prōmptus, ūs) only abl. ū, m promo+ EM-, in the phrase, in promptu, public, open, visible, manifest, before the eyes : ut (decorum) sit in promptu: ingenium in promptu habere, show his ability , S.: in promptu scrini…

promutuus.definition: prō-mūtuus adj., paid beforehand, advanced, lent in advance: insequentis anni vectigal promutuum, i. e. advanced for the next year, Cs.

prone.definition: prōnē adv. pronus, inclined, leaning, slanting ; opp. directe ad perpendiculum, Cs.

pronuntiatum.definition: prōnūntiātum ī, n P. n. of pronuntio, in logic, a proposition, axiom .

propago1.definition: prōpāgō āvī, ātus, āre pro+PAC-, to set forward, extend, enlarge, spread, increase : finīs imperi: eo bello terminos populi R. propagari, L. — To generate, procreate, engender, propagate : stirpem in centesimum annum:…

propago2.definition: prōpāgō or (of persons) propā gō inis, f pro+PAC-, a set, layer, slip, shoot : propagines nonne efficiunt, ut, etc.: adulta vitium, H.— Offspring, descendant, children, race, breed, stock, progeny, posterity : Alipedi…

propatulus.definition: prō-patulus adj., open in front, not covered, open, uncovered: in propatulo locc.—As subst n., an open place: in propatulo aedium, in the open court, L.: volgo in propatulis epulati sunt, in the courts, L.: pudicitiam…

propense.definition: prōpēnsē adv. with comp. propensus, willingly, readily, with inclination : propensius senatum facturum, L.

propensus.definition: prōpēnsus adj. with comp. P. of propendeo, hanging down, preponderant : id fit propensius.— Inclining towards, coming near, approaching : disputatio ad veritatis similitudinem propensior.— Inclined, disposed, prone, r…

properanter.definition: (properanter) adv. with comp. propero, hastily, speedily, quickly : alqd accipere, Ta.: beneficia properantius, quam aes mutuum, reddere, S.: properantius ire, O.

properantia.definition: properantia ae, f propero, a hastening, haste : ex tantā properantiā, S.: periculum ex properantiā, Ta.

properato.definition: properātō adv. properatus, quickly, speedily : ad mortem agitur, Ta.

properatus.definition: properātus adj. propero, hurried, accelerated, rapid, quick, speedy : mors, O.: gloria rerum, O.: naves, Ta.

propere.definition: properē adv. properus, hastily, in haste, quickly, speedily : Curre, T.: egredere, N.: Cumas se recepit, L.: naves onerare, S.

properipes.definition: properipēs edis, adj. properus+pes, swift of foot : dux, Ct.

propior.definition: propior ius, gen. ōris, adj. comp. (for sup., see proximus) cf. prope.—In space, nearer, nigher : portus propior, V.: tumulus, L.: Ut propior patriae sit fuga, O.: propior montem suos conlocat, S.—Plur n . as subst: p…

propositum.definition: prōpositum ī, n P. n. of propono, that which is proposed, a plan, intention, design, resolution, purpose : quidnam propositi haberet, Cs.: adsequi, to attain : propositum tenere, L.: peragere, N.: tenax propositi, H.—…

propositus.definition: prōpositus adj. P. of propono, exposed, open : omnibus telis fortunae vita; tabernis apertis proposita omnia in medio vidit, L.: oppida ad praedam, Cs.: mulier omnibus, accessible.— At hand, impending : vitae periculum.

proprie.definition: propriē adv. proprius, personally, severally, as one's own, properly, in person : parte (campi) frui: quod tu amandus es, id est proprie tuum: cuius causam neque senatus publice neque ullus ordo proprie susceperat: qu…

propter1.definition: propter adv. prope, near, hard by, at hand : ibi angiportum propter est, T.: cum duo reges propter adsint: duo filii propter cubantes: cornix volans, Ph.

propter2.definition: propter praep. with acc. 1 propter, near, hard by, next to, close to : hic propter hunc adsiste, T.: qui propter <*>e sedit: insulae propter Siciliam. —Fig., on account of, by reason of, for the sake of, through, in v…

propylaea.definition: propylaea —, n , propu/laia, a gateway, entrance; esp., the Propylaea to the Parthenon.

prorsum.definition: prōrsum adv. pro+vorsum, forwards : cursari rursum prorsum, to and fro , T.—Fig., absolutely, at all : prorsum nihil intellego, T.

proscriptus.definition: prōscrīptus ī, m P. of proscribo, an outlaw, proscribed person, one under the ban : lex, quae proscriptum iuvari vetat: in proscriptorum numero esse, S.

prospectus2.definition: prōspectus ūs, m pro+SPEC-, a lookout, distant view, prospect : cum saepibus prospectus impediretur, Cs.: prospectum ager arbustis consitis prohibebat, S.: pulcherrimo prospectu porticus: adempto propinquo congredient…

prospere.definition: prōsperē adv. prosperus, according to hope, as desired, favorably, luckily, fortunately, prosperously : quicquid gestum est: evenire: haec minus prospere procedebant, N.

prospicientia.definition: prōspicientia ae, f prospicio, foresight, forethought, precaution : vigilia et prospicientia.

proterve.definition: protervē (prō-, T.), adv. with comp. protervus, recklessly, boldly, wantonly, impudently : iracundus, T.: consectans proterve bene de re p. meritor: quicquid facias protervius aequo, O.

proventus.definition: prōventus ūs, m pro+BA-, a coming forth, growth, produce, yield : Proventu oneret sulcos, V. —Fig., an issue, result : in bello omnīs secundos rerum proventūs expectare, Cs.— A harvest, fortunate issue, happy result, …

providens.definition: prōvidēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of provideo, foreseeing, provident, prudent : homo: id est ad reliquas res providentius, in other respects more prudent : providentissimus quisque, Ta.

proviso1.definition: prōvīsō adv. 1 provisus, with forethought, deliberately : temere, proviso, Ta.

proviso2.definition: prō-visō —, —, ere, to go forth to see, see to it: proviso, quid agat Pamphilus, T.

provisus2.definition: (prōvīsus ūs), m pro+VID-.—Only abl. sing., a looking forward, distant view : ne oculi provisu iuvabant, Ta.— A foreseeing : periculi, Ta. — A caring for beforehand , Ta.

provivo.definition: prō-vīvō vīxī, ere, to live on, Ta.

proxime.definition: proximē or proxumē adv. sup. proximus. —Of place, nearest, very near, next : quam proxime potest castris, as close as possible , Cs.: exercitum habere quam proxime hostem.—Fig., of time, very lately, just before, most…

prudenter.definition: prūdenter adv. with comp. and sup. prudens, sagaciously, intelligently, discreetly, circumspectly, learnedly, prudently : res attendere, S.: facere: disputavit multa: quaestio non satis prudenter constituta: belli adm…

pruniceus.definition: prūniceus adj. prunus, of plum-tree wood : torris, O.

prytanis.definition: prytanis is, m , pru/tanis, in Greece, a member of the chief executive body, prytane, L.

psallo.definition: psallō ī, —, ere, ya/llw, to play upon a stringed instrument, sing to the cithara: elegantius, S.: Doctae psallere Chiae, H.

psithius.definition: psithius (psy-) adj. , yi/thios, of a species of Grecian vine producing a sweet wine, Psithian: vitis, V.—As subst f. (sc. vitis), V.

pte.definition: -pte enclit., added to the abl. of a pron possess., self, own: suopte pondere: suāpte manu: nostrāpte culpā, T.

ptisanarium.definition: ptisanārium ī, n ptisana, barley-groats, a decoction of barley-groats, gruel : oryzae, H.

pubes1.definition: pūbēs eris, adj. 3 PV-, grown up, of ripe age, adult, pubescent : filii: priusquam pubes esset, N.: aetas, L.— Plur m . as subst, grown-up persons, adults, men : omnes puberes armati convenire consuerunt, Cs.— Covered…

pubes2.definition: pūbēs is, f 3 PV-, grown-up males youth able to bear arms, youth, young men : Italiae: robora pubis Lecta, V.: Romana, L.: indomita, i. e. the young bullocks , V.— The youth, throng, people : agrestis, V.: captiva, H.…

publice.definition: pūblicē adv. publicus, on account of the people, publicly, officially, for the state, in behalf of the state : Haud cito mali quid ortum ex hoc sit publice, any public misfortune , T.: aurum signanto, coin : disciplin…

pudendus.definition: pudendus adj. P. of pudeo, causing shame, shameful, scandalous, disgraceful, abominable : ut iam pudendum sit honestiora decreta esse legionum quam senatus: vita, O.: volnera, V.

pudens.definition: pudēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of pudeo, shamefast, bashful, modest, shy, chaste, sensitive, honorable : filius: pudens prave, H.: animus, T.—Plur m . as subst: neque pudentes suspicari oportet sibi parum c…

pudenter.definition: pudenter adv. with comp. and sup. pudens, modestly, bashfully, shyly : respondere: vivendo: sumere, H.: pudentius accedere: pudentissime hoc petere.

pudice.definition: pudīcē adv. pudicus, modestly, chastely, virtuously : doctum ingenium, T.

pueriliter.definition: puerīliter adv. puerilis, like a child : ludentes, Ph.: blandiri, L.— Childishly, foolishly, sillily : facere.

puerperus.definition: puerperus adj. puer+2 PAR-, parturient, bringing forth children : verba, charms to aid child-birth , O.—As subst f., a woman in labor : illa, T., H.

puga.definition: pūga (pȳga) ae, f , pugh/, the rump, buttocks, H.

pugil.definition: pugil ilis, m PAC-, one who fights with the cestus, a fist-fighter, boxer, pugilist : pugilem esse (virginem) aiunt, T.: Olympionices: Illum non labor Isthmius Clarabit pugilem, H.

pugillatio.definition: pugillātiō ōnis, f pugillor, to be a boxer, boxing with the cestus, fist-fighting .

pugnaciter.definition: pūgnāciter adv. with sup. pugnax, contentiously, violently, obstinately : certare cum aliis: pugnacissime defendere sententiam.

pugnantes.definition: pūgnantēs ium, m P. plur. of pugno, fighters, warriors : species pugnantium, Cs., Cu.

pugnantia.definition: pūgnantia ium, n P. plur. of pugno, contradictions, inconsistencies, things irreconcilable : pugnantia loqui: secum componere, H.

pulchre.definition: pulchrē (pulcrē) adv. with sup. pulcherrime pulcher, beautifully, excellently, finely, nobly, very : pulcherrume dictum, T.: adseverat, bravely : proxima hostia litatur saepe pulcherrime, very favorably : mihi pulchre…

pullatus.definition: pullātus adj. 2 pullus, clothed in black, in mourning : proceres, Iu.

pullus1.definition: pullus ī, m 3 PV-, a young animal, foal, young, offspring : ranae, H.: columbini: gallinacei, L.: ciconiae, Iu.: ex ovis pulli orti, chicks.—A young fowl, chicken : mea pullis in parte catini, H.: caveā liberati pulli…

pullus2.definition: pullus adj. 2 PAL-, dark-colored, blackish-gray, dusky, blackish : ne maculis infuscet vellera pullis, V.: capilli, O.: myrtus, dusky , H.: praetor cum tunicā pullā, i. e. dressed like a common workman : toga, mournin…

pulpita.definition: pulpita orum (sing. late), n a scaffold, platform, pulpit, lecture-desk, stage: percurrit pulpita socco, H.: vati, quem pulpita pascunt, Iu., O.

puls.definition: puls pultis, f 1 PAL-, a thick pap, pottage, porridge, mush (used in sacrifices, and given to the sacred chickens): si in offam pultis invasit (avis): grandes fumabant pultibus ollae (as food of the poor), Iu.

pulsus2.definition: pulsus ūs, m 1 PAL-, a pushing, beating, striking, stamping, push, blow, impulse, stroke : pulsu externo agitari: pulsu remorum praestare, in rowing , Cs.: sonum vocis pulsu pedum modulantes, keeping time in the dance…

pulvinarium.definition: pulvīnārium ī, n pulvinus, a cushioned seat of a god : in pulvinario consedisse, L.

punctum.definition: punctum ī, n P. n. of pungo, a prick, puncture : volucris parvulae (i. e. muscae), Ph.— A point, mathematical point , C.—Since in the comitia a point upon the waxed tablet indicated the name voted for, an affirmative …

punio.definition: pūniō or poeniō īvī, ītus, īre poena, to punish, correct, chastise : ambitum: sontes: facinus puniendum: tergo ac capite puniri, L.: quod non ego punior, O.— To take vengeance for, avenge, revenge : Graeciae fana.

pure.definition: pūrē adv. with comp. purus, clearly, cleanly, brightly : lauta corpora, L.: splendens Pario marmore purius, H.— Distinctly, simply : loqui: pure apparere rem, as it is , H.— Completely, fully : Quid pure tranquillet, …

purgatus.definition: pūrgātus adj. P. of purgo, cleansed, clear : auris, i. e. open to admonition , H.

purpuratus.definition: purpurātus ī, m purpura, one clad in purple, an officer of a royal court, king's attendant, courtier : minitare purpuratis tuis: ex purpuratis regis esse, L.

pus.definition: pūs pūris, n 2 PV-, matter from a sore, pus ; hence, fig., gall, bitterness, malice : Rupili, H.

puta.definition: puta adv. imper. of puto, suppose, for instance, namely : Quinte, puta, aut Publi, H.

puter.definition: puter tris, tre, adj. 2 PV-, rotten, decaying, putrefying, stinking, putrid : quibus alabaster puter esse videtur: fanum, mouldering , H.: poma, rotten , O.: bos, O.: corpora cicatricibus, Cu.: vomicae, Iu.— Crumbling…

putide.definition: pūtidē adv. with comp. putidus, disgustingly, disagreeably, affectedly : dicere: primi litteras putidius, with nauseous precision .

putresco.definition: putrēscō —, —, ere, inch. putreo, from puter, to rot, moulder, decay : vestis putrescit, H.

pyctes.definition: pyctēs ae, m , pu/kths, a boxer, pugilist, Ph.

pylae.definition: pylae ārum, f , pu/lai, a narrow pass, defile: Tauri: Susides, Cu.

pytiso.definition: pȳtīsō —, —, āre, puti/zw, to spit out: pytisando modo mihi Quid vini absumpsit, T.
